# Test data

The go tool ignores this directory; everything here feeds the corpus and
golden tests. Drop files in, run `go test ./...` — tests discover the
content, and skip (with a notice) when a directory is empty.

## `mqtt/` — field captures

MQTT traffic captures, one file per capture session, as gzipped
newline-delimited JSON: `mqtt/<anything>.ndjson.gz`.

Each line is one MQTT message as seen on a meshcore broker:

```json
{"ts":"<RFC3339>","topic":"meshcore/<region>/<node id>/packets","b64":"<MQTT payload>"}
```

Only `…/packets` topics are consumed; `…/status` (node telemetry) is
skipped. The `b64` payload is itself JSON, published per received frame
by capture clients (meshcore firmware, meshcoretomqtt,
meshcore-packet-capture, openhop_repeater…); the fields used are:

```json
{"type":"PACKET","raw":"<full frame, hex>","hash":"<8-byte dedup hash, hex>",
 "packet_type":"<int>","payload_len":"<int>"}
```

`corpus_test.go` requires (nearly) every frame to parse and re-encode
byte-identically — field captures contain the odd RF-corrupted frame,
so up to 1% unparseable is tolerated and logged. When the reporter
attached its dedup `hash` and its own `packet_type`/`payload_len` agree
with our parse, the hash must match ours exactly; that agreement gate
exists because some clients hash their own, sometimes wrong, view of
the frame.

## `golden/` — vectors produced by the reference implementation

Golden vectors generated by the MeshCore C++ code itself, as JSON lines:
`golden/<anything>.ndjson` (optionally `.ndjson.gz`). The generator
lives in [`golden/gen/`](golden/gen/): it compiles the reference
sources (Packet, Identity, Utils, AdvertDataHelpers, the vendored orlp
ed25519 and the rweather/Crypto primitives the firmware links) into a
host binary. The repo-root Taskfile drives it against released MeshCore
sources — MeshCore has no repo-wide tags, so `repeater-vX.Y.Z` (all
per-app tags share the tree and numbering) is fetched as the canonical
source for protocol version X.Y.Z:

```sh
task golden VERSION=1.17.1 SEED=42   # one corpus
task golden:all                      # the whole supported matrix
```

Output is deterministic per (version, seed); corpus files are named
`mc-<version>-seed<n>.ndjson.gz` and the whole directory is replayed by
the tests, so several versions and seeds sit side by side. On releases
predating helpers/UTF8Helpers.h the builder truncates advert names
bytewise; the generator detects that and marks those app-data blobs
`canon:false` so only the version-stable assertions apply to them.
`make coverage` (in `gen/`) reports how much of the reference code the
sweep exercises.

One record per line, dispatched on the `test` field. Every `valid`
field records what the reference code actually returned — verdicts are
measured, never assumed. Supported kinds — this list is the contract
between `gen/main.cpp` and `golden_test.go`; update both together:

```json
{"test":"packet_roundtrip","frame":"<hex>"}
{"test":"packet_hash","frame":"<hex>","hash":"<hex, 8 bytes>"}
{"test":"packet_parse","frame":"<hex>","valid":false}
{"test":"sign","prv":"<hex, 64B expanded>","message":"<hex>","signature":"<hex, 64B>"}
{"test":"verify","pub":"<hex, 32B>","message":"<hex>","signature":"<hex, 64B>","valid":true}
{"test":"shared_secret","prv_a":"<hex, 64B>","pub_b":"<hex, 32B>","secret":"<hex, 32B>"}
{"test":"encrypt_then_mac","secret":"<hex, 32B>","plain":"<hex>","out":"<hex>"}
{"test":"mac_then_decrypt","secret":"<hex, 32B>","in":"<hex>","valid":true,"plain":"<hex, padded>"}
{"test":"advert_verify","payload":"<hex>","valid":true}
{"test":"path_return","secret":"<hex, 32B>","payload":"<hex>","valid":true,
 "path_len":3,"path":"<hex>","extra_type":1,"extra":"<hex, padded>"}
{"test":"channel","psk":"<hex, 16B or 32B>","hash":"<hex, 1B>","in":"<hex>","plain":"<hex, padded>"}
{"test":"advert_appdata","appdata":"<hex>","canon":true,"valid":true,
 "adv_type":2,"has_loc":true,"lat":48858370,"lon":2294481,
 "feat1":0,"feat2":0,"name_hex":"<hex>"}
```

`packet_roundtrip` asserts parse → re-encode is byte-identical;
`packet_hash` asserts our dedup hash matches the firmware's;
`packet_parse` asserts our accept/reject verdict matches `readFrom`'s
(frames come from crafted negatives and seeded fuzz);
`encrypt_then_mac` is deterministic (ECB, zero padding, truncated HMAC)
so full output equality is expected, and `mac_then_decrypt` includes
tampered MAC/ciphertext/key cases; `path_return` replays the receiver
pipeline (envelope split, MAC, inner path descriptor) with the fields
as the reference receiver extracts them (the reserved-descriptor
rejection vector is emitted only for firmware 1.17+, which added the
guard — `DecodePathReturn` implements that newer behavior); `channel` pins the group-PSK
semantics — hash over the PSK's real length, crypto keyed by the
zero-padded 32-byte array; `advert_appdata` carries the
reference parser's own reading of the blob, and `canon:true`
(builder-produced) blobs must also re-encode byte-identically — that is
what pinned our name truncation to the reference's UTF-8-aware
behaviour. An unknown `test` value fails the run on purpose: generator
and consumer must stay in lockstep.
